messages:
Maria L: Heads up — our March invoice from GCP has a weird accelerator charge. Looks like two different rates applied to the same instance group in asia-east2. Anyone else seeing this?
Tim O'Connor: Yikes. Can you paste the line items? :eyes:
Maria L: Here are the relevant lines from the `exported_usage.csv`:
```
project_id,sku_description,usage_start_time,usage_end_time,usage_amount,unit_price,charge_amount
prod-gpu,GPU T4 (on-demand),2026-03-01T00:00:00Z,2026-03-01T23:59:59Z,240,0.35,84.00
prod-gpu,GPU T4 (on-demand),2026-03-02T00:00:00Z,2026-03-02T04:00:00Z,40,0.35,14.00
prod-gpu,GPU T4 (reserved),2026-03-01T00:00:00Z,2026-03-01T23:59:59Z,240,0.12,28.80
prod-gpu,GPU T4 (reserved),2026-03-02T00:00:00Z,2026-03-02T04:00:00Z,40,0.12,4.80
prod-gpu,GPU T4 (on-demand),2026-03-01T23:45:00Z,2026-03-02T02:10:00Z,147.5,0.35,51.625
```
Maria L: You can see `reserved` and `on-demand` both billed for overlapping intervals. That last line is from our nodepool migration window.
Raj Patel: We saw something vaguely similar before but this looks like both SKUs were counted. Not a discount mismatch — it's double counting overlapping resource-hours.
Ashley Chen: Opened a GCP support ticket (#123456789). They asked for full invoice PDF + `exported_usage.csv` + cluster logs. I attached autoscaler logs and node lifecycle events.
DevOps Bot: deploy-billing-checker: ran reconciliation against `billing-exports.prod_gcp` — found duplicated GPU hours 2026-03-01T23:45:00Z -> 2026-03-02T02:10:00Z. Mismatch: 53.8 GPU-hours, estimated overcharge = $18,720.00. See /opt/tools/billing/reports/1764312000-dup-gpu.csv
Tim O'Connor: Can we confirm if we had simultaneous nodepools or a migration that left old nodes running while new nodes were billed? @Raj can you check the autoscaler / cluster-controller events?
Raj Patel: Checked: we created nodepool `nodepool-gpu-v2` and cordoned old `nodepool-gpu-v1` at 2026-03-01T23:45Z. Drain completed, but nodes in v1 weren't deleted until 2026-03-02T02:10Z due to a stuck detach of local SSDs. That explains overlap.
Maria L: If the cloud billed both the reserved commitment and on-demand for the overlap, we need a refund and reallocation of the commitment. @Billing Bot can you confirm commitment allocation rules for this project?
Billing Bot: Commitments are applied at the project + SKU level in our current setup. However the usage exporter shows two SKUs: `GPU T4 (on-demand)` and `GPU T4 (reserved)` for the same hours. GCP billing support notes this can happen if instances are temporarily flagged with a different SKU (e.g., migrating between nodepool types). I've opened an internal finance ticket and cc'd finance@redwood.com.
Ashley Chen: I pushed the autoscaler logs and node-delete timestamps to the GCP ticket; support escalated to billing review. Their ETA is ~72h. I also requested a provisional credit for the overlapping window.
Tim O'Connor: Short-term: let's add a safety check to prevent overlapping billed hours next time. Proposal: after we cordon+drain, delete node pool only after confirmation of no attached block devices or after 15 minutes. I'll draft a PR for a pre-delete hook. :hammer_and_wrench:
Maria L: Also please run a quick historical scan for similar SKU overlaps over the last 6 months. If this is a recurring pattern we need a policy change. Raj, can you run `./scripts/billing_diff.sh --sku "GPU T4" --window 180d` and paste results?
Raj Patel: Running now, will post a short summary in this thread when done.
Tim O'Connor: Thanks. Keep finance looped on the ticket ID and any interim credit offers.
Maria L: Filing internal postmortem checklist: ACTIONS: 1) Confirm GCP credit + adjusted invoice 2) Implement pre-delete guard 3) Run 6mo scan + report 4) Add alert if reserved vs on-demand usage overlap > 1h.
Raj Patel: Quick follow-up (after scan): only this March 1-2 window showed SKU overlap. Total suspected overcharge ~$18.7k. Logged follow-up in finance tracker: FT-2026-042.
Maria L: Great — thanks everyone. I'll update execs once GCP responds.
